primary.reference_chain: GPS -> u-blox ZED-F9T TP1 PPS (falling edge) -> i210 SDP0 -> ts2phc -> PHC -> chrony -> CLOCK_REALTIME

stamp.why: CLOCK_REALTIME is disciplined to the PHC by chrony; reading it costs far less than reading the PHC, and the discipline error is orders of magnitude below the read cost.

discipline.reference: u-blox ZED-F9T TP1 PPS -> i210 SDP0

mesh_crosscheck.what: i210 PHC continuously measures the P550-BMC PHC (ptp4l free_running=1, slaveOnly=1 -> read-only instrument; it never steers the i210)

witness.hardware: SpacemiT K3 Pico ITX, stmmac PHC /dev/ptp1
witness.reference_chain: GPS -> LEA-6T -> P550-BMC GPS grandmaster (PTP domain 44, UDPv4) -> ptp4l -> PHC -> chrony -> CLOCK_REALTIME
witness.why_not_independent: The witness's grandmaster (the P550-BMC PHC) is CONTINUOUSLY MEASURED by the same i210 that carries the primary time base — see primary.mesh_crosscheck. The two chains meet at a monitored junction, so this is a watched peer inside one mesh, not a second opinion from outside it.

stamp.why: CLOCK_REALTIME is disciplined to the PHC by chrony; reading it costs far less than reading the PHC, and the discipline error is orders of magnitude below the read cost.

gnss_source.role: This receiver's TP1 PPS is the electrical input that ts2phc uses to discipline the i210 PHC. The telemetry below characterises that very signal; it is read from the timehat database, not asserted.
gnss_source.coupling: TP1 PPS (falling edge, 100 ms) -> coax -> i210 SDP0 -> ts2phc -> /dev/ptp0. Separately, UBX over UART -> qerr_logger.py on f9t -> timehat.qerr_stream and timehat.rawx_stream.
gnss_source.sawtooth_is_NOT_applied: ts2phc runs with a generic PPS source and no sawtooth correction; nothing reads qErr back to correct the i210. The qErr below is therefore an UNCORRECTED residual inside the i210's error budget, not a correction already in effect.

qerr_latest.meaning: UBX-TIM-TP sawtooth: how far the TP1 edge that ts2phc latched on the i210 SDP0 fell from its ideal instant

rawx_latest.leap_note: RAWX leapS is GPS-UTC. TAI-GPS is a fixed 19 s, so TAI-UTC = leapS + 19. This is the leap offset as broadcast by the satellites, independent of the host kernel's adjtimex value.
rawx_latest.why_published: Satellite count and constellation mix are an integrity signal: a consistent multi-constellation fix is materially harder to spoof than GPS alone. This is a health indicator, not a proof.

cross_check.interpretation: This delta is NOT a measurement of the offset between the two time bases. Both stamps were fetched over SSH and the difference is dominated by acquisition skew, bounded above by acquisition_skew_bound_ns. A real comparison requires a simultaneous triggered capture, not two SSH calls.
cross_check.independence: NOT independent, and deliberately so. The witness's grandmaster is watched continuously by the primary's i210 (mesh_crosscheck), which is what makes the witness trustworthy rather than merely separate. Residual shared-mode risk: both chains start at GPS, so neither covers a constellation-wide fault or spoofing. Different receivers (ZED-F9T vs LEA-6T), boards, and servos (ts2phc vs ptp4l) do cover receiver-local faults.
cross_check.why_the_crosscheck_matters: Over 21 days the ZED-F9T logged 0 qErr excursions beyond 50 ns in 357,982 samples (sd 2.255 ns). The LEA-6T that feeds the BMC has a comparable core (sd 6.02 ns) but produced 3 excursions past 1 us in 468,631 samples. Rare multi-microsecond excursions on the witness chain are exactly what the continuous i210-vs-BMC measurement is there to expose.

precision.what_bounds_the_stamp: the cost of reading the clock, not the clock's quality
precision.error_budget_note: The receiver's sawtooth sd is ~2.26 ns while the delivered i210 discipline is ~8.3 ns RMS. Removing the sawtooth in quadrature would leave ~8.0 ns, so the receiver is NOT the dominant term — the PPS cable, the SDP0 latch and the servo are. Do not describe this as a 2 ns system.
precision.honest_summary: The primary clock is disciplined to GNSS at the nanosecond level, but this stamp was read from userspace at a cost of ~9999 ns. Treat the stamp as good to MICROseconds. The nanosecond figures describe the clocks; they are not the accuracy of this timestamp.
uncalibrated_terms: GNSS antenna cable delay (69 ns configured in the F9T; unverified by us)
PPS coax length from F9T TP1 to i210 SDP0
i210 SDP0 input latency / edge-detect offset
receiver accuracy with respect to UTC(k), both receivers
PTP path asymmetry on the witness chain (path delay ~893 ns, one-way assumed)

disclosure.signed_payload: sha256 of canonical(core); all signatures cover the same digest
disclosure.what_this_proves: Integrity since signing, attested by three independent hosts on two independent GNSS receiver chains.
disclosure.what_this_does_NOT_prove: It does not prove the value was unknown before publication. Single publisher, no external anchor. Any draw that matters must combine a pulse with a participant-supplied nonce.
disclosure.time_precision_vs_accuracy: We claim precision and a traceable discipline chain, NOT calibrated absolute accuracy versus UTC(k).
disclosure.not_certified: Not NIST/FIPS/CC validated. Not an accredited service. See CLAIMS.md.
